coverageDimensions:
SERVICE coverage would mean: which AWS services' activity these foundational sources let GuardDuty observe. The page gives you nothing measurable. It names the three log-producing services (AWS CloudTrail, Amazon VPC, Route 53 Resolver), which is an inventory of sources, not of monitored services. For the monitored side it says only "services that support CloudTrail" — an unbounded reference with no list — and the five global services (IAM, AWS STS, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon Route 53) are introduced by "For global services such as", an illustrative set, restated three sentences later as only three of the five. There is no denominator and no exhaustive numerator, so no service ratio can be computed from this page.

REGION coverage would mean: in which AWS Regions foundational data source monitoring is available. The page gives you nothing. Exactly one Region string appears on the whole page, `us-east-1`, and it appears inside a Note as an example of a finding's Region field differing from the detection Region — it is a worked example, not a supported-Region entry. The page makes only unquantified assertions: monitoring begins "when you enable GuardDuty ... in a Region", and global service events are processed "in all Regions where you've enabled the service, including both default and opt-in Regions". Region availability for GuardDuty lives on a different page; do not synthesise a Region list here, and do not read "default and opt-in Regions" as an enumeration.

RESOURCE TYPE coverage would mean: which resource types these sources produce telemetry about. The page gives you nothing enumerable, only informal scoping nouns inside prose: VPC Flow Logs cover "network interfaces attached to the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances"; DNS query logs apply to "your Amazon EC2 instances"; and Lambda functions are mentioned only via the Lambda Protection cross-reference, which is a different feature. These are two or three resource nouns scattered in sentences, with no list, no CloudFormation/ARN type identifiers, and no universe to measure against. Turning "EC2 instance" and "Lambda function" into a resource-type coverage figure would be fabrication.

Plainly: of the three dimensions, this page supplies none. It supplies exactly one usable thing — a closed, self-published list of three data sources, with two conditional exclusions on the third.

features.reasoning: This is the only set on the page that can be enumerated and to which a reach-or-not-reach statement is actually attached. The axis values are log/event stream types, so "dataSource" is exact — they are not services (CloudTrail the service is not the same value as CloudTrail management events; VPC Flow Logs is a feature of Amazon VPC, not Amazon VPC), not resource types, and not Regions. The axisKind is catalogue, not external, and this is the load-bearing call: "foundational data sources" is a grouping GuardDuty publishes about itself. GuardDuty decides what belongs on the list, so it holds 3 of 3 by construction and a 100% figure would be meaningless as coverage. The individual values do point at external log types (CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, Resolver DNS query logs) drawn from a much larger universe of AWS log types — CloudTrail data events, S3 server access logs, ELB access logs, CloudFront logs, Route 53 public DNS query logs and so on — but the page never enumerates that universe, so there is no denominator to divide by. The correct use of these 3 values is as an inventory of what GuardDuty ingests for free by default, and as input to a service-level map (which AWS services' telemetry GuardDuty sees), never as a ratio. Note also that Lambda Protection and GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring appear here only as cross-reference blocks explaining scope and billing interactions; they are separately-enabled paid features documented on their own pages and are explicitly not foundational data sources, so they must not be added as a fourth or fifth value.
features.scope: Per AWS Region in which GuardDuty is enabled — the page states monitoring is per-Region and that CloudTrail global service events are replicated into every enabled Region (default and opt-in), but it names no Regions, so this second dimension has no enumerable values here.
features.statuses: 3 of 3 stated as supported, 0 stated as not supported. There is no Yes/No column; support is asserted by the framing sentence "After you enable GuardDuty in your AWS account, it automatically starts to monitor the log sources explained in the following sections" plus one H2 section per source. Counted two ways and both give 3: the Topics block lists 3 anchors, and there are 3 content H2s (AWS CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, Route53 Resolver DNS query logs) before the "See also" boilerplate — the Topics block and the H2s are the same three items, not two lists to add up. The page carries two genuine NEGATIVE statements, but neither removes a value from this list: (1) "If you use another DNS resolver, such as OpenDNS or GoogleDNS, or if you set up your own DNS resolvers, then GuardDuty cannot access and process data from this data source"; (2) a Note — "GuardDuty doesn't support monitoring DNS logs for Amazon EC2 instances that are launched on AWS Outposts because the Amazon Route 53 Resolver query logging feature is not available in that environment." Both are conditional caveats scoping the Route53 Resolver DNS query logs entry, and neither comes with an enumerable universe (resolvers are given as "such as" examples; Outposts is a single named environment with no sibling list), so they must be recorded as qualifiers on that one value, not as a second axis and not as "not covered" entries. Other sentences containing "not"/"doesn't" are disclaimers about GuardDuty not managing or altering the customer's own CloudTrail and flow-log configuration, and a billing note that GuardDuty will not charge twice when Runtime Monitoring is active — none of these are coverage exclusions.

shouldNotExtract: The Topics block (a table of contents duplicating the three H2s — treating it as a separate list double-counts to 6). The "See also" section in its entirety, including the boilerplate bullet about Skills for AI coding assistants and the `aws agent-toolkit search-skills` command that AWS now appends to every page. The billing and pricing paragraphs: the 30-day free trial, estimated monthly usage per data source, delegated administrator cost breakdown, AWS Billing, "There is no additional cost", and the Runtime Monitoring double-charge-avoidance note — pricing is not coverage. The three "examples of CloudTrail management events" bullets (IAM `AttachRolePolicy`, Amazon EC2 `CreateSubnet`, AWS CloudTrail `CreateTrail`) — explicitly labelled examples, and API operations are not services or resource types. The five global services introduced with "such as" — an illustrative set, not a supported-services list. The single Region string `us-east-1` in the Note. The Lambda Protection and GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring cross-reference blocks, which describe separately-enabled features documented elsewhere. The disclaimers that GuardDuty does not manage or alter the customer's CloudTrail, flow log, or Resolver query logging configuration — these say nothing about reach. All outbound documentation links.
trap: The page reads like an enumeration page but its only real enumeration is three items long, so a careless parser fills the gap with the wrong lists. The single most likely mistake is harvesting the five global services from "For global services such as AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS), Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Amazon CloudFront, and Amazon Route 53 (Route 53)" and emitting them as five services covered by GuardDuty CloudTrail monitoring. That sentence is explaining why global events get replicated across Regions; "such as" makes it non-exhaustive, and the very same paragraph restates the set as only three, so any parser that grabbed it would also produce an unstable count between runs. The close second is emitting `us-east-1` as a supported Region from the Note, when the Note exists to warn that a finding's Region field can disagree with the detection Region. Third, a parser that keys on bullets will lift the three "examples of CloudTrail management events" as an API-operation or service axis, or will add the Topics block to the H2 sections and report 6 data sources. Fourth, it will promote the Lambda Protection and Runtime Monitoring cross-reference blocks into the data source list, giving 5 — they are separately-enabled features, and the page's whole point is that foundational sources need no enablement. Finally, and most consequentially for a coverage map: even a parser that correctly extracts 3 of 3 may present it as "100% data source coverage". That number is true by construction, because GuardDuty itself decides what a foundational data source is, and publishing it as a coverage ratio is misleading.
whatThePageStates: The page defines what GuardDuty calls its "foundational data sources" — the log and event streams GuardDuty ingests automatically, with no extra enablement and no extra cost, once GuardDuty is turned on in a Region. It enumerates exactly three: AWS CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, and Route53 Resolver DNS query logs, each with a section explaining how GuardDuty consumes it through an independent duplicated stream that does not touch the customer's own CloudTrail/flow-log/Resolver configuration. The rest is billing framing (30-day free trial, no additional cost), an explanation of how CloudTrail global service events are replicated into every Region where GuardDuty is enabled, and two exclusions on the DNS source. It contains no tables, no Region list, no service list, and no resource-type list.
